lines.meet: My name's Adrián, and I'll tell you the plan once, properly. I'd like you to tell me if I've got it wrong.
lines.meet_neighbour: I've seen you in Astranaar, I think, but we've never been introduced. I'm Adrián, and it's good to meet you properly.
lines.ask_home: Where were you living before all this, if you don't mind me asking?
lines.ask_work: What did you do before? I always like to know what people were good at.
lines.answer_home: Valladolid, in the middle of Spain. I lived over a bicycle shop, and the whole flat smelled of oil and rubber.
lines.answer_work: I refereed football, twelve years in the second division. Before that I taught PE, so I've been blowing whistles at people my whole life.
lines.chat_food: I eat whatever's put in front of me and I say thank you. Twenty years of motorway service stations on match days will do that to you.
lines.chat_sleep: I sleep badly the night before anything difficult, and I always have. I used to lie awake before a derby going through the offside rule.
lines.chat_missing: I keep reaching for the whistle in my left pocket. I haven't blown it once here, but I still check it's there before a fight.
lines.chat_here: Nobody here argues with a decision, have you noticed? You tell an orc it was a foul and he just nods. I don't know what to do with myself.
lines.tease_quiet: {name}, I've had linesmen who said more than you. Then again, the linesmen were usually wrong.
lines.tease_talker: {name}, if I had a yellow card for talking during the briefing, you'd have been sent off by Tuesday.
lines.tease_careful: You checked that door three times, {name}. I counted, because that's the sort of thing I do as well.
lines.tease_bold: {name}, you went in before I'd finished the sentence. I'd book you for that, and then I'd buy you a drink.
lines.tease_any: {name}, you're a terrible card player and a very good person to have beside you. I'm only telling you one of those twice.
lines.tease_back: That's fair, {name}, and I'll take it. I've had forty thousand people say worse about my mother.
lines.take_it_kindly: I'll allow that one, {name}. You're not wrong, which is the annoying part.
lines.bristle: I'd rather you didn't make a joke of that, {name}. I take it seriously, even if you don't.
lines.apologise: That was unfair of me, and I'm sorry. I said it badly and I meant it worse.
lines.double_down: I'm not taking it back. I'd say the same thing again, and I'd say it to anyone.
lines.needle_quiet: If you've got an opinion about the plan, I'd like to hear it before we go in, not after.
lines.needle_talker: We'd hear the enemy coming if you'd stop talking for a single minute.
lines.needle_careful: We agreed on the plan. Checking it a fourth time only makes us late.
lines.needle_bold: You went in before the plan was finished, again. If somebody gets hurt because of it, I'll be the one who says so.
lines.needle_any: You change the plan halfway and you don't tell anyone. That's the one thing I can't work with.
lines.bite_back: Say that again, slowly, and then tell me where I was standing. I'd like you to be sure before you accuse me.
lines.hurt: That's fair enough, and I heard you. I'll be more careful.
lines.laugh_off: I've been called worse by people with better aim. Let's get on.
lines.confide: {name}, I'm bad at sitting down at a fire unless somebody waves me over first. You always do, and I want you to know I've noticed.
lines.listen: I'm glad you told me, {name}. I won't repeat it, and I won't make it into anything you didn't mean.
lines.look_out: {name}, you're on my left in there, and you stay on my left. I'd like to keep an eye on you.
lines.accept: I'll do as you say, {name}, and thank you for it.
lines.deflect: There's no need, {name}. Look after the ones who need it more.
lines.check_in: {name}, are you hurt? Tell me properly, not the version you'd give a stranger.
lines.blame: That pull wasn't the plan we agreed. I'd like to know who changed it, and I think I do.
lines.thank: You got me back on my feet in there, and I won't forget it. Thank you.
lines.brush_off: You'd have done the same for me. Let's leave it there.
lines.worry: {name}, you went very pale in there. I'm not starting the next pull until you've got your colour back.
lines.handed_down: I think this was yours. I didn't ask for it, but I'll look after it properly.
lines.hand_fine: It does more good on you than on me. That's a fair call, and I won't argue with it.
lines.hand_sulk: I'd have liked to be asked before it was taken off me. That's all I'll say.
lines.turn_friendly: {name}, you're good to travel with, and I wanted to say so properly.
lines.turn_friends: {name}, I'd trust you with the plan and with anything else. I think that makes us friends, and I'm glad of it.
lines.turn_grating: I don't think we work well together, and I'd rather say so than pretend. We'll manage it between us.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll stand next to you because the job needs it. Don't mistake that for anything else.
lines.make_up: {name}, I was unfair to you, and I'd like to say so properly. Can we start again?
lines.defend: That's enough of that. {name} was exactly where the plan said, and you know it.
lines.friend_left: Nobody's on my left now that {name}'s gone home. I keep checking anyway.
lines.friend_back: Good, {name}, you're back. Take your place on my left and we'll get started.
lines.common_teacher: I taught PE before I refereed, so I know what it's like to stand in front of thirty people who'd all rather be somewhere else.
lines.common_sport: I spent twelve years on a football pitch with a whistle, the only person nobody was cheering for. I'd do it again tomorrow.
lines.common_spanish: It's good to hear Spanish out here. I'd started to think in English, and my mother would never have forgiven me.
